arguments.explanation: All three reimbursement-chain elements are now extracted and present: merchant invoice TEST-INV-800006 from Oak Kitchen 006 (DOC-56120427, net/tax/payable 2,130.73, ref REF-20261006); personal payment slip PAY-00006 (DOC-76678915) showing "Paid personally by Employee 006 (TEST)" for the same invoice/ref; and employee expense claim REF-20261006 (DOC-61909067, Employee 006, 2,130.73). Bank row TX-00007 (-213,073 cents, 2026-10-27, counterparty "Employee 006 (TEST)", memo "REF-20261006 settlement part 1") matches reference, counterparty and amount, and paying the employee is the correct direction for a reimbursement per policy. The only failing check is REIMBURSEMENT_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH on DOC-76678915: the check expects the payment slip's 'issuer' to be "Oak Kitchen 006 (TEST)" but the extraction records issuer = "Employee 006 (TEST)" (payer) and recipient = "Oak Kitchen 006 (TEST)" (merchant). This is a role-mapping discrepancy in a payer/payee document, not an absence of the merchant fact — a re-extraction returned the same values, faithful to the source text. I will not flip roles just to satisfy the check, and the amount (2,130.73) and reference (REF-20261006) do match on all documents, so this is not an unsupported difference in facts. I did not achieve a passing check, so I am escalating rather than producing a draft. Note the bank memo says "settlement part 1"; only one bank row exists and it alone equals the full amount, so no duplicate/partial-payment issue appears, but a human may confirm.
questions: For payment slip DOC-76678915 (PAY-00006), should the merchant 'Oak Kitchen 006 (TEST)' be recorded as the issuer and 'Employee 006 (TEST)' (the personal payer) as the payer/recipient, or should I keep the payer/payee orientation (issuer = Employee 006, recipient = Oak Kitchen 006)? The deterministic check requires issuer = Oak Kitchen 006.

Bank row TX-00007 is memoed 'REF-20261006 settlement part 1' but its full -2,130.73 equals the entire reimbursement; please confirm there is no second partial payment to Employee 006 for REF-20261006 before I finalize a single full-amount reimbursement entry (debit 660202 / credit 1002, 213,073 cents, no input tax).

arguments.explanation:
The evidence itself is complete and internally consistent, but the deterministic checks keep failing on party/acceptance matching with no diagnostic details, so I cannot build a draft and will not force one.

What the sources show (all for REF-20261016):
- DOC-50930305 — Invoice TEST-INV-800016, Clearview → Orion Technology 016 Ltd (TEST), 2026-10-16, net 148,238 + tax 8,894 = 157,132 cents.
- DOC-37107474 — Engagement letter signed 2026-10-16 between Clearview (provider) and Orion Technology 016 (client); total 157,132 cents; permits a 40% split payment; states completion needs separate client acceptance.
- DOC-78002172 — Client acceptance dated 2026-10-26, From Orion Technology 016 Ltd To Clearview, confirming the report and handover were received/accepted, no outstanding deliverables, total 157,132 cents.
- Bank: TX-00017 (62,852) + TX-00018 (94,280) = 157,132 cents, both memo "REF-20261016 settlement part 1/2" and counterparty Orion Technology 016 Ltd (TEST). Policy allows combining split payments when reference and counterparty agree.

So the substantive policy conditions for revenue look satisfied: contract present, separate client acceptance present, payment fully settled, totals agree, no duplicate.

Actions taken that did not clear it:
1. Extracted the two unparsed documents (contract and acceptance); UNPARSED_EVIDENCE cleared.
2. Set classification = revenue with a verbatim invoice quote; UNCERTAIN_CLASSIFICATION cleared.
3. Re-extracted DOC-78002172 because the first pass had issuer/recipient reversed relative to the document text ("From: Orion ... To: Clearview"). Corrected.
4. Re-extracted DOC-37107474 to refresh its party/description fields.
5. Re-ran check_case: still ACCEPTANCE_MISMATCH, BANK_PARTY_MISMATCH, PARTY_MISMATCH, with an empty details array.
6. Searched all sources for REF-20261016 and Orion: only these three documents exist, no conflicting party or amount, and no lookalike row matches (e.g. TX-00066 is Orion Technology 061, a different reference REF-20261061).

Source facts were not altered to fit the totals and no entries were posted.

My best reading is a checker-side party-normalisation problem rather than a business problem: the documents spell the counterparty "Orion Technology 016 Ltd (TEST)" everywhere, yet the checker treats it as a mismatch. But I cannot verify that from here, and policy forbids posting when facts conflict or checks fail, so this goes to a human.

For the acceptance DOC-78002172, should the accounting treatment require the accepting party to be recorded as the client (Orion Technology 016 Ltd (TEST)) and the recipient as Clearview, and does the checker expect that orientation or the reverse?

The contract DOC-37107474 is a two-party agreement signed by both sides; should it be recorded with issuer = Clearview and recipient = Orion, or is a neutral/bilateral party representation expected by the PARTY check?

If the checker failure is confirmed to be a normalisation defect rather than a real discrepancy, do you approve proceeding to build_draft for revenue (debit 1002 157,132; credit 6001 148,238; credit 222102 8,894)? This still requires your approval and would not be posted automatically.

One substantive issue remains and blocks a draft: MISSING_ACCEPTANCE. Policy states "Service revenue requires a contract AND separate client acceptance for this benchmark," and the contract itself says "Completion requires a separate client email or signed delivery confirmation. An invoice or bank receipt alone is not proof of acceptance under this test policy." I searched the full evidence collection and there is no acceptance email, signed delivery confirmation, or completion evidence for REF-20261088 — the other 14 matching documents are engagement letters/statements of work for unrelated references (REF-20261034, -079, -061, -097, -004, -090, -013, -052, -095, -067, -089, -007, -040, -070). Note: bank memo says "settlement part 1", while TX-00089 is the full 677.10 and no second payment appears. This is not a problem (the contract allows a split payment, and one full settlement satisfies the price), but human awareness is useful.
